text: Osmanthus fragrans-derived hierarchically porous carbons for high-performance supercapacitors
Changhao Wu1,3, Yuying Qin1,2, Ze Zhao1,2, Guohe Zhang1, Zhentao Bian1,2,3*, Xuanxuan Zhao1,2*, Liying Fang1, Yunyu Sun1,2, Ligang Zhang1,2, and Keying Zhang1,2*

The microstructure and physicochemical properties of the carbon materials were systematically characterized using advanced analytical techniques. Morphological evolution was investigated by field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM, Hitachi SU-8010, Japan) operated at 5 kV with EDX mapping capability, combined with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM, JEOL JEM-2100F, Japan) at 200 kV accelerating voltage. Crystalline structure analysis was conducted via X-ray diffraction (XRD, Rigaku SmartLab 9kW, Japan) with Cu Kα radiation (λ = 1.5406 Å) at 2° min-1 scan rate, complemented by Raman spectroscopy (Thermo Fisher DXR2xi, USA) using a 532 nm laser with 1 μm spot size.

Porosity characteristics were quantitatively evaluated via N2 physisorption measurements at 77 K using a Micromeritics ASAP 2020 HD (USA). The specific surface area (SBET) was calculated via the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) method over a relative pressure (P/P₀) range of 0.05-0.30, while pore size distribution (PSD) was determined using non-local density functional theory (NLDFT) models appropriate for carbonaceous materials. Surface chemistry was analyzed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS, Thermo Scientific Escalab 250Xi, USA) with monochromatic Al Kα source (1486.6 eV). Binding energies were calibrated against adventitious carbon (C 1s = 284.8 eV) with ±0.2 eV resolution.

The electrochemical measurements were conducted using a CHI760D electrochemical workstation in a three-electrode test system, comprising a working electrode, a counter electrode (Pt plate), and a reference electrode (Hg/HgO). All tests were performed in 6 M KOH or 1 M Na2SO4 electrolyte at room temperature.
